interactionRules.effect: Increased bleeding risk; requires pharmacist/prescriber review.

source.title: Data Sheet – Coumadin – 3-Mar-2026
source.currentnessNote: The source also states warfarin doses require individual monitoring; this rule does not assess INR, prescribed dose, or personal risk.

interactionRules.evidenceSummary: The Coumadin New Zealand data sheet lists concomitant NSAID use among circumstances associated with serious bleeding risk and recommends ongoing clinical monitoring.

interactionRules.effect: Concomitant use is contraindicated because PDE5 inhibitors can potentiate the blood-pressure-lowering effects of nitrates.

source.title: VIAGRA – New Zealand Data Sheet
source.currentnessNote: The cited product label is sildenafil-specific; the ruleset applies its curated PDE5 class mapping and does not verify every product label.

interactionRules.evidenceSummary: The Medsafe data sheet states that sildenafil potentiates nitrate-related hypotension and contraindicates co-administration with organic nitrates or nitric-oxide donors.

interactionRules.effect: Concomitant use is contraindicated because of the risk of serotonin syndrome.

source.title: Sertraline HCl Capsules – U.S. FDA Prescribing Information (2023)
source.currentnessNote: This U.S. label states it may not be the latest FDA-approved labeling. The class-wide SSRI mapping and current New Zealand labeling require clinician verification.

interactionRules.evidenceSummary: The cited sertraline label contraindicates concomitant use with MAOIs and describes serotonin-syndrome risk.

interactionRules.effect: Trimethoprim alone or in co-trimoxazole with methotrexate can cause severe bone marrow suppression. Prompt pharmacist/prescriber review is required.

source.title: Interaction reminder: Bone marrow suppression with methotrexate and trimethoprim or co-trimoxazole (3-Mar-2022)
source.currentnessNote: The article describes case reports and monitoring advice; the ruleset does not assess dose, indication, timing, blood tests, or an individual plan.

interactionRules.evidenceSummary: Medsafe reports severe, sometimes fatal, bone-marrow suppression with methotrexate plus trimethoprim or co-trimoxazole, and advises avoiding the combination where possible.

interactionRules.effect: May cause severe hyperkalaemia, especially with renal impairment. Requires clinical review and potassium/renal monitoring.

source.title: Reminder: Hyperkalaemia caused by Spironolactone and Renin-angiotensin System Medicine Interactions (1-Sep-2016)
source.currentnessNote: Medsafe marks the article as more than five years old and says content may no longer be current; confirm against current product information.

interactionRules.evidenceSummary: Medsafe says severe hyperkalaemia risk should be considered with spironolactone plus ACE inhibitors, especially with renal impairment, and recommends potassium/renal monitoring.

interactionRules.effect: Can increase simvastatin exposure and cause serious muscle injury/rhabdomyolysis. Prompt pharmacist/prescriber review is required; route and formulation must be checked.

source.title: Simvastatin Interactions and Fatal Reports (15-Dec-2014)
source.currentnessNote: Medsafe marks the article as more than five years old and says content may no longer be current. The present class mapping must be checked against current datasheets.

interactionRules.evidenceSummary: Medsafe describes potentially life-threatening myopathy/rhabdomyolysis with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors and contraindicates that combination in the cited article.

interactionRules.effect: Increased risk of serotonin syndrome. Requires pharmacist/prescriber review.

source.title: Opioids and serotonergic medicines: some combinations may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome (1-Sep-2022)
source.currentnessNote: The cited source stratifies specific opioid classes and combinations; this grouped warning is conservative and does not assess an individual regimen.

interactionRules.evidenceSummary: Medsafe describes risk as varying by opioid/antidepressant combination and identifies tramadol, pethidine, and dextromethorphan as high risk with serotonergic antidepressants.

interactionRules.effect: Concomitant use is contraindicated because of serotonin syndrome risk. Prompt pharmacist/prescriber review is required.

source.title: Opioids and serotonergic medicines: some combinations may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome (1-Sep-2022)
source.currentnessNote: The source identifies particular high-risk opioids; product identity and serotonergic class mapping must be confirmed.

interactionRules.evidenceSummary: Medsafe identifies concomitant use of high-risk serotonergic opioids with MAOIs as contraindicated in its risk table.
